newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors to summon politicians on Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors to summon politicians on Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors plan to question politicians who have been named by the founder of the stricken Hanbo Group as allegedly taking his bribes, a prosecution official said on Wednesday.
He said prosecutors had a list of politicians Chung Tae-soo had confessed to paying off, but declined to give any details.
"All politicians in the Chung Tae-soo list will be summoned for questioning," the official said. "When and how they will be investigated will be decided later."
In testimony broadcast live from a Seoul jail on Monday, Chung told a parliamentary inquiry his officials gave money to three politicians -- one each from the ruling party and two opposition groups.

Domestic media reports say Chung has a list of about 20 politicians he is alleged to have bribed to keep loans rolling in to Hanbo's steelmaking flagship, which ultimately collapsed in January after new money dried up.
Chung is on trial on bribery and other charges along with nine others in connection with the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co.
